prerequisites: analysis: 1st and 2nd order differential equations with constant coefficients

learning_outcomes.text: Students can explain the basic principles of electricity.
Students can explain the electrical behavior of the ideal elements from electrical network theory.
Students can independently calculate all electrical properties of linear electrical networks for both AC and DC.
Students can explain the basic principles of transfer functions.

syllabus_topics: Series and parallel connection of resistors
Practical session: review exercises of DC theory
Chapter 7 - First and second order circuits
Chapter 8 - AC analysis in steady state
Phasors and the various circuit elements
Practical session: review exercises of AC theory - variable frequency
Exercise 1: resistive networks + practical: measuring V/I/R
Exercise 2: nodal analysis + practical: measuring amplifier with VDI
Exercise 3: first and second order networks + practical: measuring step responses
Exercise 4: AM receiver + practical: testing AM receiver
assessment_rules: The exam is written and consists of 20 to 25 multiple-choice questions. Multiple-choice questions are corrected with a penalty for guessing. The total number of points is reduced to 20. The exam duration is 3 hours. No formula sheet is allowed, but a calculator conforming to faculty guidelines is permitted.
bibliography: Irwin D., Nelms R., "Basic engineering circuit analysis - tenth edition", John Wiley and Sons.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
